description: Curated swimming training principles for AI-assisted plan generation. Derived from publicly available USMS training guidelines, British Swimming coach education materials, and established sports science literature on swimming periodization.

zones.z1: Aerobic — comfortable, conversational effort. Develops aerobic base and technique.
zones.z2: Threshold — comfortably hard, sustained effort. Builds lactate threshold and race pace endurance.
zones.z3: High intensity — hard, unsustainable beyond short efforts. Develops speed and power.

recommended_drills.name: kickboard kick
recommended_drills.purpose: leg strength and horizontal body position

key_principles: Prioritise water confidence and basic technique over volume
Keep rest intervals generous (20–30s) so technique does not break down
Short reps (1–4 lengths) allow full technique focus on each rep
At least one kick-focused set per session to build leg strength
Increase volume before increasing intensity

periodization.pattern: Flat load — consistent volume each week, drills rotate

recommended_drills.name: catch-up drill
recommended_drills.purpose: stroke timing and front quadrant swimming

recommended_drills.name: fist drill
recommended_drills.purpose: forearm awareness in the catch phase

recommended_drills.name: 3-3-3 drill
recommended_drills.purpose: structured rotation and stroke count awareness

key_principles: Low volume — quality of each stroke matters more than distance covered
Long rest intervals allow full mental reset between drill reps
Alternate drill and swim reps to transfer technique immediately
Focus on one technique cue per session, not multiple at once
Count strokes per length to track efficiency improvement

periodization.pattern: 2 weeks base, 1 week introduce speed work, repeat

recommended_drills.name: sprint with full rest
recommended_drills.purpose: introduce fast turnover, 1 length at a time

key_principles: Build aerobic base first — speed without base leads to injury and poor form
Speed reps must be short (1–2 lengths) with full rest so quality is maintained
Never sprint more than 10% of total session volume at beginner level
Focus on stroke rate increase, not stroke length shortening

periodization.pattern: 3-week build, 1-week taper. Final week: 60–70% of peak volume, maintain intensity
taper_principles: Reduce volume by 30–40% in final week
Maintain intensity — do not cut speed work
Include at least one race-pace set in taper week

key_principles: Include at least one race-pace set per week from week 2 onward
Practise turns and starts in every session — race time is won on the walls
Taper volume but not intensity in the final week
Underwater dolphin kicks off every wall are high-value for beginners — practise daily

recommended_drills.name: pull buoy freestyle
recommended_drills.purpose: isolate upper body, build pull strength

recommended_drills.name: descending set
recommended_drills.purpose: negative split training and pace awareness

key_principles: Main sets should be continuous aerobic efforts — 200–400m equivalent blocks
Introduce threshold sets (Z2) from week 2 onward at 15–20% of volume
Pull buoy sets twice per week build pull power without adding leg fatigue
Negative split every main set — first half slower than second half

periodization.pattern: 2 weeks aerobic base, 2 weeks speed development, 1 week recovery, repeat

key_principles: Speed sets require FULL rest — do not cut rest on sprint reps
Underwater dolphin kicks off every wall are critical for speed — minimum 3–5 kicks
Include one threshold set (Z2) and one speed set (Z3) per session in build weeks
Volume is secondary to quality — do fewer reps at proper speed rather than more at reduced pace

periodization.pattern: Focus on one technique element per week. Weeks rotate: catch → pull → rotation → kick → turns

recommended_drills.name: catch-up drill
recommended_drills.purpose: front quadrant swimming and stroke timing

key_principles: One focal technique point per session — not multiple cues simultaneously
Alternate drill rep and full-stroke rep to immediately transfer the skill
Track stroke count per length to measure efficiency gains over weeks
Cooldown should include slow, deliberate swimming with the session's technique focus

periodization.pattern: 3-week build, 1-week taper. Include race-pace sets from week 1.
taper_principles: Reduce volume by 35% in final week
Keep all intensity — cut reps, not pace
Include one full race-pace simulation set
Shorten warm-up in taper week sessions

recommended_drills.name: race-pace sets
recommended_drills.purpose: develop and cement target pace feel

recommended_drills.name: broken swims
recommended_drills.purpose: experience race pace with minimal rest

key_principles: Every session from week 1 should include at least 4 lengths at goal race pace
Underwater dolphin kicks after every turn — aim for 5–7 kicks minimum
Practise race-start dive or push-off in every session if pool permits
Mental race rehearsal: visualise the race during the last 100m of main set

periodization.pattern: 3 weeks progressive load, 1 week deload. Mesocycle: 4 weeks base, 4 weeks build.

key_principles: Main sets are long continuous blocks: 400–800m equivalent at Z1/Z2
CSS (critical swim speed) should anchor all threshold sets
Deload weeks must genuinely reduce volume — advanced swimmers often overtrain during recovery
Long cooldown is essential for recovery at this training load

periodization.pattern: 2 weeks base, 2 weeks speed, 1 week recovery. Rotate mesocycles.

key_principles: Sprint sets must use full rest — never shorten rest to fit more reps
Underwater dolphin kicks: 7–10 kicks from every wall, maximum power
Speed sessions require 48h recovery — schedule carefully across the week
Max velocity work (Z3) should not exceed 15% of weekly volume

periodization.pattern: Each week targets one technical system: catch mechanics → body rotation → kick timing → breathing pattern → turns and walls

key_principles: At advanced level, small technique gains yield large time improvements
DPS (distance per stroke) is the key metric — track strokes per length every session
Pair drill with threshold swimming to test technique retention under effort
Turns and walls: every push-off is a technique opportunity — never coast

periodization.pattern: 4-week build, 1-week peak, 1-week taper. Race-pace sets mandatory from week 1.
taper_principles: Reduce volume by 40% in final week
All intensity sessions maintained — cut reps not pace
One full race simulation on day 4 of taper week
Sharpening sprint sets (3–4 x 1 length max effort) on day 2 of taper

recommended_drills.name: CSS descending sets
recommended_drills.purpose: building to and beyond race pace

recommended_drills.name: 15m underwater from push
recommended_drills.purpose: maximise underwater phase at race speed

key_principles: Underwater dolphin kicks: 7–10 powerful kicks from every wall — race margins live here
Every session includes race-pace exposure — no session is purely aerobic in race prep
Peak week: highest intensity, not highest volume
Taper without losing sharpness: reduce length of sets, keep the pace targets
